name: Lymecycline

sources.citation: FDA Philippines product-registration data preserved in the website registry; exact generic/product records inspected November 25, 2026. Cached record, not a new verification of current registration validity.

Galderma Philippines/Sophartex. Tetralysal(lymecycline)300 mg capsule Philippine package insert, DR-XY 29605, revised May 29, 2023. Retrieved from FDA-registration PI link and verified November 25, 2026. Each capsule 408 mg lymecycline, equivalent to 300 mg tetracycline base.
Galderma UK. Tetralysal 300 mg Hard Capsules SmPC; emc updated August 12, 2026. Verified November 25, 2026. Foreign regulatory comparator, not substituted for local insert.

Dubertret L, et al. The use of lymecycline in the treatment of moderate to severe acne vulgaris: a comparison of the efficacy and safety of two dosing regimens. Eur J Dermatol.2003; 13(1):44–48. PMID 12609781.

draft_notes: No inferred CKD-band, HD, PD or CRRT regimen. Current Philippine product identity/insert governs applicability.

revision_log.change: Source-verified descriptive evidence and explicitly attributed regulatory guidance; numerical recommended doses only from verified exact local insert.
revision_log.approved_by: W. G. M. Rivero, MD (delegated source-verification workflow; executed by Codex, 2026-11-25)

usual_adult_dose.dose: 300 mg/day; usual duration 12 weeks. Capsule: 408 mg lymecycline equivalent to 300 mg tetracycline base [[LYMPH]]
600 mg/day; adequate fluids reduce esophageal injury [[LYMPH]]

contraindications: Tetracycline/component hypersensitivity; age under 8 years; oral retinoids; pregnancy/lactation (Philippine insert) [[LYMPH]]

serious: Intracranial hypertension, photosensitivity; high-dose nephrotoxicity and overdose hepatotoxicity [[LYMPH]]

monitoring: Stop for suspected intracranial hypertension; avoid expired tetracyclines because renal tubular acidosis can occur [[LYMPH]]

key_interactions.drug_or_class: Iron, antacids/mineral salts, sucralfate and other listed absorption-interfering agents

evidence.title: Local insert and clinical evidence
evidence.intro: Exact Philippine product instructions are separated from foreign regulatory text and research regimens.

rows.findings: The exact Philippine and UK inserts have different renal-restriction wording; see the kidney-specific section.
rows.limitations: This difference is reported rather than resolved into a universal renal contraindication or numerical reduction. Verify local insert and patient circumstances.

rows.design: 271 patients; 12-week placebo-controlled comparison of two daily regimens.
rows.intervention: Lymecycline 300 mg once daily versus 150 mg twice daily or placebo; study protocol.
rows.findings: Once-daily treatment was noninferior to twice-daily treatment and superior to placebo; reported drug-related adverse events were similar across groups.
rows.limitations: Acne trial, not evidence of safety in kidney failure or all susceptible infections.

renal: Exact Philippine insert: caution with renal/hepatic impairment [[LYMPH]].
UK comparator additionally contraindicates overt renal insufficiency; jurisdiction wording differs and is not resolved into a universal contraindication here [[LYMUK]].
No numeric CKD, HD, PD or CRRT regimen is established by the cited sources [[LYMPH,LYMUK]].
